::: {.why}
You assumed an exponent of one half on day 149 and have been carrying that assumption through every capacity estimate since; today it becomes a measurement with an uncertainty.
:::

## What you should be able to do tonight

- Estimate the impact exponent from your own data with a confidence interval.
- Say what a linear model would have predicted differently at ten times your typical size.

## Tasks <span class='task-total'>60 min</span>

::: {.task-list}
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [35 min]{.task-min} Fit it properly: regress log impact on log participation with the volatility scaling from the Toth paper included, and report the exponent with a standard error. Then check robustness across symbols, across days and across participation ranges, since a single pooled estimate can be driven by one liquid name.
:::
::: {.task}
<input type="checkbox" class="task-check"> [25 min]{.task-min} Compare the implications: at your fitted exponent against an exponent of one, compute the cost of a trade at one percent, five percent and twenty percent of daily volume. The divergence at large size is the reason the exponent matters more than the coefficient.
:::
:::

## The running strategy

::: {.project}
The impact exponent and coefficient in qlib/costs.py are replaced by values fitted to real data with a stated uncertainty, which retires the largest assumption in every cost and capacity number reported since week 22.
:::

## Resources

- [Tóth et al. (2011) — Anomalous price impact and the critical nature of liquidity](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.1694) [paper]{.res-kind}
- [Amihud (2002) — Illiquidity and stock returns](https://www.cis.upenn.edu/~mkearns/finread/amihud.pdf) [paper]{.res-kind}

## Deliverable

::: {.deliverable}
A fitted impact exponent with a confidence interval and robustness across symbols, wired into qlib/costs.py.
:::

## Checkpoint

::: {.checkpoint}
Why is impact closer to the square root of size than to linear? Give your fitted exponent, its interval, and one mechanism.
:::
